info.name: VectorPattern
info.comment: Provides support for the filling and stroking of vectors with patterns.

description.p: The VectorPattern class is used by Vector painting algorithms to fill and stroke vectors with pre-rendered patterns. It is the most efficient way of rendering a common set of graphics multiple times.

The VectorPattern must be registered with a VectorScene via the VectorScene.AddDef() method. Any vector within the target scene will be able to utilise the pattern for filling or stroking by referencing its name through the Vector.Fill and Vector.Stroke fields. For instance url(#dots).

A special use case is made for patterns that are applied as a fill operation in VectorViewport objects. If the pattern is a single tile that covers the viewport, which is the default when Units is BOUNDING_BOX, X and Y are zero, Width and Height are 100% and no Transform is set, the renderer will dynamically render the pattern as a background within the viewport. This ensures that the pattern is rendered at maximum fidelity whenever it is used, and not affected by bitmap clipping restrictions. It should be noted that this means the image caching feature will be disabled.

Any other configuration is tiled within the viewport in the same way as a vector fill, with the viewport serving as both the bounding box and the user space of the pattern. User space coordinates are therefore relative to the viewport's top-left corner.
It is strongly recommended that the VectorPattern is owned by the VectorScene that is handling the definition. This will ensure that the VectorPattern is deallocated when the scene is destroyed.

field.name: AspectRatio
field.comment: Controls how the viewport's viewbox is fitted to the pattern tile.

description.p: The AspectRatio determines how the source area defined by the Viewport's ViewX, ViewY, ViewWidth and ViewHeight fields is scaled and aligned within each pattern tile. It is equivalent to the preserveAspectRatio attribute of SVG patterns. The default value is MEET|X_MID|Y_MID, which scales the content uniformly so that it fits within the tile and centres it. Use SLICE to fill the tile while clipping the overflowing content, or NONE to stretch the content independently on each axis.

The AspectRatio is only effective if a viewbox has been defined for the Viewport. It controls the fitting of content within a tile and has no effect on the tile's dimensions or position, which are determined by X, Y, Width, Height and Units.
This field is a convenient alias for the AspectRatio of the pattern's Viewport, and the two always report the same value.

field.name: ContentUnits
field.comment: Defines the coordinate system for the content of the pattern.

description.p: ContentUnits declares the coordinate system of the vectors in the pattern's Viewport. The default setting is USERSPACE, in which content coordinates are expressed in the same units as the pattern tile. If set to BOUNDING_BOX, content coordinates are expressed as fractions of the bounding box of the vector that is consuming the pattern, e.g. a coordinate of (0.5,0.5) refers to the centre of that bounding box. In this case the content is stretched independently on each axis and the AspectRatio has no effect. The mapping is always relative to the consumer's bounding box, regardless of the Units setting.
In compliance with SVG, ContentUnits has no effect if a viewbox has been defined in the Viewport. The viewbox determines the content's coordinate system in that case.

The (Width,Height) field values define the dimensions of the pattern tile. If the provided value is scaled, then the dimension is calculated relative to the bounding box or viewport applying the pattern, dependent on the Units setting.

field.name: Inherit
field.comment: Inherit attributes from a VectorPattern referenced here.

description.p: Attributes can be inherited from another pattern by referencing it in this field. This feature is provided primarily for the purpose of simplifying SVG compatibility and its use may result in an unnecessary performance penalty.

field.name: Matrices
field.comment: Applies one or more transforms to a pattern.

description.p: A transform can be applied to a pattern via one or more matrices. These will influence how pattern fills are rendered within their vector space. Each matrix is represented by a VectorMatrix structure, and the matrices are linked in the order in which they should be applied.
The opacity of the pattern is defined as a value between 0.0 and 1.0, with 1.0 being fully opaque. The default value is 1.0.

field.name: Scene
field.comment: Refers to the internal VectorScene that will contain the rendered pattern.

description.p: The VectorPattern class allocates a VectorScene in this field and inherits its functionality. In addition, a VectorViewport class will be assigned to the scene and is referenced in the Viewport field for managing the vectors that will be rendered.

field.name: SpreadMethod
field.comment: The behaviour to use when the pattern bounds do not match the vector path.

description.p: Indicates what happens if the pattern starts or ends inside the bounds of the target vector. The default value is VSPREAD::PAD.

field.name: Transform
field.comment: Applies a transform to the pattern during the render process.

description.p: A transform can be applied to the pattern by setting this field with an SVG compliant transform string.

field.name: Units
field.comment: Defines the coordinate system for fields X, Y, Width and Height.

description.p: This field declares the coordinate system that is used for values in the X, Y, Width and Height fields. The default setting is BOUNDING_BOX, which means the pattern tile is sized relative to the bounding box of each vector that uses it. With USERSPACE, the tile size is independent of the consumer, which makes it the most efficient choice when a pattern is shared by vectors of different sizes.
In both cases the tile is rendered at its scale on the display, including any scaling from Transform, and it is cached until the definition or that display size changes.

field.name: Viewport
field.comment: Refers to the viewport that contains the pattern.

description.p: The Viewport refers to a VectorViewport object that is created to host the vectors for the rendered pattern. If the Viewport does not contain at least one vector that renders an image, the pattern will be ineffective.

The renderer manages the transform and size of the Viewport so that it matches each pattern tile. Defining the Viewport's ViewX, ViewY, ViewWidth and ViewHeight fields establishes a viewbox for the pattern content, which is fitted to the tile according to the AspectRatio.

The (Width,Height) field values define the dimensions of the pattern tile. If the provided value is scaled, the dimension is calculated relative to the bounding box or viewport applying the pattern, dependent on the Units setting.
The (X,Y) field values define the starting coordinate for mapping patterns.
The (X,Y) field values define the starting coordinate for mapping patterns.
